newsitem.title: USA: Medtronic says FDA clears Wiktor stent.
newsitem.headline: Medtronic says FDA clears Wiktor stent.

text.p: Medtronic Inc said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration cleared the Wiktor coronary stent for commercial marketing.
Distribution of the device to U.S. interventional cardiologists will begin immediately and continue as centers complete training, said the medical devices maker.
Coronary stents are implanted in coronary arteries to hold them open after angioplasty procedures.
The booming U.S. market for stents has been dominated by Johnson & Johnson, but FDA clearance of the Wiktor opens a new phase in which rivals such as Medtronic will challenge J&J, analysts said.

The Wiktor is indicated for implantation when a coronary artery or bypass graft vessel has been opened by percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty, or PTCA, and is at risk for abrupt or threatened closure, when the PTCA procedure alone fails to restore complete blood flow to the heart muscle, Medtronic said.
Medtronic said it estimated that about 170,000 coronary stents were used in the United States during 1996.
During a stent procedure, many patients receive more than one device, with the U.S. average about 1.3 stents per person.
The Wiktor stent was co-developed by Medtronic with electrical engineer Dominik Wiktor of Cranford, N.J.
The stent was commercially released in Europe and other countries in 1992.
